svg.text: Structured output — a grammar automaton masks each position’s illegal tokens, then renormalises

g.text: Start at state S0. The grammar permits only the opener. Legal set = { {"x": }.
Singleton legal set ⇒ mask is a no-op; opener sampled with p=1, appended. Advance S0→S1.
At S1 the model wants a digit. Unconstrained softmax favours } (0.644) — illegal here.
WITHOUT masking, } would be sampled → invalid {"x":}. The constraint engine forbids this path.
Mask the 3 illegal logits to −∞; softmax renormalises over the survivor → 7 at p=1.000. Sample 7, append. Advance S1→S2.
At S2 only the closer is legal; singleton set ⇒ forced p=1. Sample }, append. Advance S2→S3 (accept).
Accept state reached. Output {"x":7} is complete and grammar-valid. The clock loops to a fresh generation.

svg.text: each sampled token rides its rail down to the output
CONTROL STRUCTURE — grammar automaton (the outer loop over positions)
loop: advance to the next position, run the body again
LOOP BODY — one generation step (worked at S1: the digit decision)

g.text: legal set has size 1 ⇒ masking leaves one survivor,
softmax renormalises it to p = 1.000 — forced by construction,
no logit arithmetic needed. (The rich case is the digit decision above.)
every position emitted exactly one legal token;
the automaton reached its accept state S3.

svg.text: bright circle = current state · dim = past/future
masking removes the illegal tokens and redistributes their probability mass
across the legal ones in proportion to what they already had (e^−∞ = 0).
Multi-token case: when ≥2 tokens are legal, the same mask-then-renormalise keeps their relative proportions.
Here every position has exactly one legal token, so each distribution collapses to p = 1.000.
